sections.h2: What React Native healthcare app development is, and when we choose it
paras: React Native healthcare app development means building your app in Meta's React Native framework: JavaScript or TypeScript, one codebase, compiled to real native components on Android and iOS. Elevate Aura uses it whenever the app is one part of a larger platform that also has a web dashboard and a shared backend.

The clearest example is Carna Medicare, a medical-equipment distributor in Chennai. Their 12-module operations platform includes a field-staff app in React Native, a manager dashboard, GST billing, payment tracking and service tracking, all on Supabase, with a WordPress site alongside. The whole platform shipped in 30 days, and the app and dashboard share data models and logic because they share a language.
When the app is a standalone, interface-heavy product with no JavaScript around it, Flutter may be the better call. We advise on that before scope is fixed.

sections.h2: When the app and the dashboard are built by different people in different languages.
sections.lead: Healthcare and distribution apps rarely live alone. They report to an office dashboard, and that is where the trouble starts.

items.p: The app calls it a visit, the dashboard calls it a call, and the fields do not line up.
Validation rules, GST calculations and status flows are coded once in the app and again on the web, and drift apart.
A bug that crosses the app and the dashboard bounces between two teams who each blame the other.
Your in-house developers write JavaScript, and the app was built in something they cannot read.
A new field on the job card needs a change in three places by three people.

sections.h2: React Native healthcare app development, answered.

items.q: What have you built in React Native?
items.a: The Carna Medicare field-staff app, part of a 12-module operations platform with a manager dashboard, GST billing, payment tracking and service tracking, on Supabase with a WordPress site. It shipped in 30 days. The Aura Business mobile app follows the same pattern.

The screens use the platform's own native components, so the app looks and behaves like an Android app on Android and an iOS app on iOS. The business logic is written once in JavaScript or TypeScript.

items.q: Can it share code with our web app?
items.a: Yes, when the web app is in JavaScript. Data models, validation rules and API clients are shared with a Next.js dashboard, which is the main reason we choose React Native for platform builds.

items.q: Does it handle offline mode and GPS?
items.a: Yes. Offline storage with background sync, GPS check-in, camera, barcode scanning and signature capture are all standard parts of the field apps we build in React Native.
You do. The repository is handed over with documentation, and any JavaScript developer can work on it. Support from the builder continues on WhatsApp.

items.q: When would you not recommend React Native?
items.a: When the app is a standalone, design-heavy product with no JavaScript web platform beside it, or when your team already works in Dart. Then we suggest Flutter, which we have also shipped to Google Play.
